candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the MAOI-related OTC dextromethorphan warning.

options.A: Do not use dextromethorphan while taking an MAOI or for 2 weeks after stopping the MAOI unless specifically directed by a qualified clinician.
options.B: Take dextromethorphan at double the usual dose.
options.C: Dextromethorphan has no relevant interaction warning with MAOIs.
options.D: Use it only if the cough lasts more than 7 days.

candidate.rationale: Current OTC dextromethorphan labeling states not to use the product while taking a prescription MAOI or for 2 weeks after stopping the MAOI. The warning is explicit and does not depend on the duration of the cough.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Dextromethorphan must not be used with an MAOI or within 2 weeks after stopping one.
candidate.source_locator: Drug Facts—Warnings: Do not use with a prescription MAOI or within 2 weeks after stopping
candidate.stem: A client taking a prescription monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) asks to use OTC dextromethorphan for cough. What should the nurse advise?
